## Design

### 2026-10-23 – 22 OCT-OCT24: PCB design.

**12h**

22 OCT-OCT24: PCB design.

The first thing I did this time was open the guide created by Hack Club members. I downloaded symbols, footprints, and and 3d models required for the project and successfully added them to KiCad.

With this, I can start designing the schematic, but before that I had to make a choice: either use the XIAO ESP32-S3 or the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Zero. I found the S3 on Amazon. So I am sticking with it for now.

Next, I am going to choose the other parts of the keypad: Capacitive Touch Keys, Low-Profile Switches, EC11 Rotary Encoder, Bourns Slide Potentiometer, which are the same parts used in the guide; however, I am going to change the orientation and number of parts. My vision is to create a MIDI keypad similar to AKAI MPK Mini MK3. However, after some research, the Mini MK3 has too many keys, which are way more than the number of GPIO pins on the Esp32. So I will be reducing the number of keys by quite a bit. I also found this keypad (nanoKEY 2 - Black KORG), which has a very cool configuration, in my opinion.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/a0ea8659fc60a86f1eb25ef982620f67b40c2337171a911ba215a31ace1df999.png)

I will be using half the Keys on this board, which are about 13 keys. Adding to the other switches and other components, the number of required GPIO pins is more than what my microcontroller can handle, so I will be searching for another one with more GPIO pins.

I found the ESP-WROOM-32 dev kit to be perfect, as it has 38 pins, which is quite a lot. But I still need to download the schematic and footprint & 3d model for this board. After a while, I found everything on GitHub. However, it has old .lib files that I can't add to my current KiCad version. I spent 30 minutes trying to fix this problem, with no success, until I accidentally pressed the arrow next to Add existing library, which showed me a menu containing the option to select a legacy library.

https://github.com/MightyMirko/esp32_devkit_38Pins

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/98fba6acc72ab8561236f2074ee25c269bc647adbc4d6b11944e3ce4f37f830d.png)

I spent a while searching for this board on Amazon and other places, but couldn't find it. For now, I will just connect the parts and figure it out this out later.

I found the 30-pin ESP-32S 30Pin Development Board on an online store. So, I am going with this one finally. I have spent some time modifying the schematic of the other board to match this one; this is the result.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/c6ecd8433f2f3607e2a794ee130900e18871772c7a6bef72606d6e742c3348d7.png)

This board supports 9 capacitive touch keys; I was planning on adding 13 of them, but I wasn't lucky, ig. I connected them to Pins (8,9,12,13,14,16,23,24,26).

The next thing to add is 3 rotary encoders, 4 switches, and 2 slide potentiometers. And here is the schematic and connections

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/7f97a843748edc6a0f2f3c7e8d9dd80151a4fad68f1ba0fbe8711b544d7f1aa9.png)

I modified the schematic a bit, and since the switches are connected to input-only pins, a resistor must be connected in parallel with the switches, so I added just that and cleaned the schematic a bit. With this, the schematic is done for now.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/f33a1f692704bc4540bf31f4bcfb0335e327078883ce14a7b95fb82174eedc68.png)

Before proceeding to design the PCB, I will assign the footprints first. The footprint for the 30 ESP32-WROOM-32S was missing, so I downloaded it from GitHub

https://github.com/syauqibilfaqih/ESP32-DevKit-V1-DOIT

now for the rest of the components,

 EC11 rotary encoder → Rotary_Encoder:RotaryEncoder_Alps_EC11E-Switch_Vertical_H20mm)

the sliding Potentiometers, I chose a 20 mm potentiometer for the project. →
Potentiometer_THT:Potentiometer_Bourns_PTA2043_Single_Slide

10k resitors → R_Axial_DIN0207_L6.3mm_D2.5mm_P10.16mm_Horizontal

For the buttons, I found some mechanical keyboard switches that are perfect.
Button_Switch_Keyboard:SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB

And finally, for the capacitive touchpad, this will be designed separately. I will organize all the components, as I need some dimensions to start on the pad design.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/91d900977ad6752460a49f242d59026fd4b1fd9ebf4e129956ecd7a0b4ea2ac8.png)
this is the orientation of the pcb for now, and it covers about 145 x 50 mm, with this in mind, i will create the foot pint the same size as the pacb or smaller by 20mm, i really liked the design of the nano key 2, but i don't think it will suit the project, as i think it is more of a switch than a key, and also i found this keypad image, which looks absolutly fantasitc.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/30c9ee67077ece225f427a07cd7b29188323e4fc2c5214a31c4992782d380ab8.png)

### 2026-10-24 – In the last session i faced a problem routing the PCB, the connections were mixed up, i traced the problem to the custom ESP32 Footprint i downloaded, all the pins are mixed up

**4h**

In the last session i faced a problem routing the PCB, the connections were mixed up, i traced the problem to the custom ESP32 Footprint i downloaded, all the pins are mixed up

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/a2656c12bf9aff79f5d99c70b1397e7767607f8d36a60df73e19b225d27cd0cb.png)

fixing this problem was simple, I just changed the Pad number in the Footprint to match that of schematic. i also changed the capacitive touch key footprint to be from 9 to 1 instead making the lower keys from 1 to 5 and the upper keys from 6 to 9. basically i just adjusted it to match the schematic, here is a screenshot after routing the keys.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/ef7d181ba4810e8c3b4f9d1d7349bdb7efca5c3bcf574aee2d4db1d2ebedd73d.png)

I continued routing the PCB, I faced some problems with the components, but i used the shcematic to wire them diffrently, basicly i was inversing the GPIO pins of the switches, encoders and so on. I had some problems with the power pin having no name, but naming it to +3.3V in both the symbol editor and the Footprint editor fixed the problem. With this done, the PCB routing is fully finished, Here is the final result.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/bc95c905e0ef81ced637ba20578512b8906874fa90aa2d6860dbeb0fd6987e0c.png)

I Spoke too soon, checking the DRC revealed 27 errors, which is a lot. However, almost all of them are caused by the capacitive touch keys' custom footprint, and after checking, the same errors are present in the hack club guide, and I think i should just Ignore those.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/si7oUujLPcQATsL6MYHnfHND9xDBNL6K/b76d494f021b9b76511057a45234b5c48fbe1291138fe563b5fa9267e93aabbd.png)

now its time for the 3d models, the process was tedious but straight forward. and something i should mention is the model for the 20mm slider was rotated in a strange manner, so I edited it in fusion. after fixing the model, It was another model for the 15 mm slider, I tired editing the model in fusion to be 20cm but it came out of proportions, how i have no Idea, i redid the whole thing again, this time i succeeded, YAAAY. finally for the ESP 32 i found this beautiful model here.
https://www.printables.com/model/1362332-esp32-devkit-v1-board-30-pin/files
